newsitem.title: FRANCE: New EU deadline to show Africa wheat deals Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: New EU deadline to show Africa wheat deals Nov 15.

text.p: Traders who have made provisional applications for long-term licences to export European Union wheat to a group of African countries have until 1400 GMT on November 15 to show the contracts and get their refunds, EU grain industry sources said on Friday.
The EU grain panel meeting on Thursday had initially set a deadline of November 13 but later changed it to November 15, they explained.

The applications are for licences valid until June 30 under so-called Article Nine EU rules that require traders to show proof of sale. The refunds were set at 12 Ecus per tonne until December and 19 Ecus per tonne from December onwards.
The EU grain panel in Brussels also decided no new offers would be accepted for these two refunds.
On October 18 traders had made provisional applications for licences to export between 294,000 tonnes and 1.054 million tonnes of EU soft wheat by June 30 under the special refunds.
Traders have said the deadline for the contracts was tight and the EU would be hard pressed to sell more than 500,000 tonnes of wheat to Africa under the scheme.
Officials said on Thursday the EU meanwhile had accepted bids for some 150,000 tonnes of wheat for export to Africa at 12 Ecus under a short-term scheme which does not require proof of contract.
